library(haven)

### Problem 1
## a. Download and Read File
```{r}
download.file("https://wwwn.cdc.gov/Nchs/Data/Nhanes/Public/2015/DataFiles/AUX_I.xpt", "AUX_I.XPT", mode = "wb")
download.file("https://wwwn.cdc.gov/Nchs/Data/Nhanes/Public/2015/DataFiles/DEMO_I.xpt", "DEMO_I.XPT", mode = "wb")

aux <- read_xpt("AUX_I.XPT")
demo <- read_xpt("DEMO_I.XPT")

dim(aux)
dim(demo)
names(aux)
names(demo)
```

merge into a dataframe

AUXTWIDR	Tympanometric width, right ear
AUXTWIDL	Tympanometric width, left ear

```{r}
attr(aux$AUXTWIDR, "label")
attr(aux$AUXTWIDL, "label")
# check these labels are about Tympanometric
summary(aux$AUXTWIDR)
summary(aux$AUXTWIDL)
# check the number of NA's
```

```{r}
aux_s <- aux[, c("SEQN", "AUXTWIDR", "AUXTWIDL")]
names(aux_s) <- c("SEQN", "tymp_r", "tymp_l")

demo_s <- demo[, c("SEQN", "RIAGENDR", "DMDCITZN", "DMDHHSZA", "INDHHIN2")]
names(demo_s) <- c("SEQN", "gender_raw", "citizen_raw", "children_raw", "income_raw")
# get data with only labels we need for AUX and demo
```

```{r}
data <- merge(
  x = aux_s, 
  y = demo_s, 
  by = "SEQN", 
  all = FALSE
)
# merge AUX and demo
```

```{r}
dim(data)
# Display the dimensions of the data.frame
```

## b. Clean the Variables

```{r}
table(data$gender_raw, useNA = "always")
table(data$citizen_raw, useNA = "always")
table(data$children_raw, useNA = "always")
table(data$income_raw, useNA = "always")
summary(data$tymp_r)
summary(data$tymp_l)
# check if there are any weird numbers like 999
```

```{r}
data$tymp_r <- as.numeric(data$tymp_r)
data$tymp_l <- as.numeric(data$tymp_l)

data$tymp_r[data$tymp_r %in% c(555, 777, 999)] <- NA
data$tymp_l[data$tymp_l %in% c(555, 777, 999)] <- NA
# recode special numbers as NA

data$tymp_r[!is.na(data$tymp_r) & (data$tymp_r < 0 | data$tymp_r > 499)] <- NA
data$tymp_l[!is.na(data$tymp_l) & (data$tymp_l < 0 | data$tymp_l > 499)] <- NA
# the value must be in the range of 1 ~ 499

summary(data$tymp_r)
summary(data$tymp_l)
# we check the summary again but we can see that there are no invalid value
```

```{r}
data$gender_raw[data$gender_raw %in% c(7, 9)] <- NA
data$gender <- factor(
  data$gender_raw, 
  levels = c(1, 2), 
  labels = c("male", "female")
)
# convert gender to a factor with informative labels.
# male is the first level

data$citizen_raw[data$citizen_raw %in% c(7, 9)] <- NA
data$citizen <- factor(
  data$citizen_raw, 
  levels = c(1, 2),
  labels = c("citizen", "noncitizen")
)
# convert citizenship status to a factor with informative labels.

data$children_raw[data$children_raw %in% c(7, 9)] <- NA
data$children <- as.numeric(data$children_raw)
data$citizen[!(data$children %in% 0: 3)] <- NA
# convert the number of young children to an ordinary numeric variable.

data$income_raw[data$income_raw %in% c(12, 13, 77, 99)] <- NA
income_midpoint <- c(
  "1"  = 2500,
  "2"  = 7500,
  "3"  = 12500,
  "4"  = 17500,
  "5"  = 22500,
  "6"  = 30000,
  "7"  = 40000,
  "8"  = 50000,
  "9"  = 60000,
  "10" = 70000,
  "14" = 87500,
  "15" = 100000
)
data$income <- unname(income_midpoint[as.character(data$income_raw)])
# convert detailed income categories to approximate dollar midpoints.
# codes 12 and 13 are broad categories that cannot be mapped uniquely.
# codes 77 and 99 are documented missing-value codes.
# all four codes therefore become NA in the continuous variable.

# replace special value in all variables with NA

table(data$gender, useNA = "always")
table(data$citizen, useNA = "always")
table(data$children, useNA = "always")
table(data$income, useNA = "always")
```

## c. Fit Poisson Model

```{r}
modelrp1 <- glm(
  tymp_r ~ gender, 
  data = data, 
  family = poisson(), 
  na.action = na.omit
)
modelrp2 <- glm(
  tymp_r ~ gender + citizen + children + income, 
  data = data, 
  family = poisson(), 
  na.action = na.omit
)
modellp1 <- glm(
  tymp_l ~ gender, 
  data = data, 
  family = poisson(), 
  na.action = na.omit
)
modellp2 <- glm(
  tymp_l ~ gender + citizen + children + income, 
  data = data, 
  family = poisson(), 
  na.action = na.omit
)
# construct four Poisson models

summary(modelrp1)
summary(modelrp2)
summary(modellp1)
summary(modellp2)
```

produce a table
```{r}
irr <- function(model, model_name){
  coef_table <- summary(model)$coefficients
  beta <- coef_table[, "Estimate"]
  se <- coef_table[, "Std. Error"]
  p_value <- coef_table[, "Pr(>|z|)"]
  data.frame(
    model = model_name, 
    predictor = rownames(coef_table), 
    IRR = exp(beta), 
    CI_lower = exp(beta - 1.96 * se), 
    CI_upper = exp(beta + 1.96 * se), 
    p_value = p_value, 
    row.names = NULL
  )
}

irr_result <- rbind(
  irr(modelrp1, "1R - Right ear: gender"), 
  irr(modelrp2, "2R - Right ear: adjusted"), 
  irr(modellp1, "1L - Left ear: gender"), 
  irr(modellp2, "2L - Right ear: adjusted")
)
irr_result
```

calculate model statistics
```{r}
pseudo_r2 <- function(model){
  1 - model$deviance / model$null.deviance
}

model_list <- list(
  "1R: Right ear, gender" = modelrp1,
  "2R: Right ear, adjusted" = modelrp2,
  "1L: Left ear, gender" = modellp1,
  "2L: Left ear, adjusted" = modellp2
)

model_statistics <- data.frame(
  model = names(model_list), 
  N = sapply(model_list, nobs), 
  pseudo_R2 = sapply(model_list, pseudo_r2), 
  AIC = sapply(model_list, AIC), 
  row.names = NULL
)
model_statistics
```
